_why: The design FORCE each pattern answers — the Minto complication, and what a recall differential discriminates on when two patterns share a situation (Factory and Builder both answer 'constructing an object'). Curated by hand, exactly like situations.json, because it cannot be derived from the README: these were authored straight into patterns.json, which meant the extractor could not reproduce its own committed artifact and every regeneration silently dropped all 187.

causes.abstract-document: readers are compiled against fixed classes, so every new property forces a change in every class that reads it
causes.abstract-factory: creating members of a family one by one lets incompatible variants be mixed, and nothing enforces family consistency
causes.active-object: method execution and method invocation share the caller's thread, so a slow method blocks every caller
causes.actor-model: shared mutable state needs locks, and locks compose into deadlocks and races as the component count grows
causes.acyclic-visitor: adding an operation to a hierarchy either modifies every class or makes every visitor depend on every type, and both couplings grow quadratically
causes.adapter: the interface a caller expects and the interface the class provides disagree, and neither side can be changed
causes.ambassador: resilience concerns (retry, timeout, monitoring) do not belong to the calling code, and inlining them duplicates the same handling at every call site
causes.anti-corruption-layer: a foreign model's concepts leak into the local model and distort it, and every shared term drifts toward the foreign meaning
causes.arrange-act-assert: a test whose setup, action and verification are interleaved cannot show which behaviour it pins, so failures do not localize
causes.async-method-invocation: the caller's thread is held hostage for the whole duration of work it does not need to watch
causes.backends-for-frontends: one general API must serve clients with conflicting needs, so it grows toward the union of all of them and fits none
causes.backpressure: the producer's rate is not coupled to the consumer's, so the difference accumulates as unbounded buffering
causes.balking: honouring a request in the wrong state corrupts the object, and making callers check first races with the state changing
causes.bloc: widgets mutate UI state directly from many places, so no single point can explain or replay how the state was reached
causes.bridge: inheritance welds abstraction to implementation, so every new pairing multiplies subclasses
causes.builder: the object's optional parts combine combinatorially, so constructors per combination cannot scale and long parameter lists hide which field is which
causes.business-delegate: presentation code knows how services are looked up and invoked, so every service change ripples into the UI layer
causes.bytecode: behaviour compiled into the program cannot be changed, sandboxed or supplied by non-programmers at run time
causes.caching: the same expensive computation repeats with unchanged inputs, so cost scales with requests rather than with change
causes.callback: the point where caller-supplied work must run is inside a routine the caller cannot reach
causes.chain-of-responsibility: binding the sender to one handler couples it to the handling structure, which must be free to change
causes.circuit-breaker: every call to a failing dependency pays the full timeout before failing, so the failure's cost multiplies instead of being cut off
causes.clean-architecture: business rules depend on frameworks and infrastructure, so a technology choice ossifies into the domain
causes.client-session: the server's own fields cannot hold per-client state without breaking statelessness and horizontal scaling
causes.collecting-parameter: each contributing method returns a partial result, and the merging logic duplicates at every call site
causes.collection-pipeline: nested loops express the mechanics of iteration, and the actual sequence of transformations is invisible inside them
causes.combinator: fixed hand-written combinations cannot cover rules that must be assembled at run time from smaller ones
causes.command: a request that exists only as a method call cannot be queued, logged, undone or scheduled — it has no reified form
causes.command-query-responsibility-segregation: one model must serve reads and writes whose shapes and loads conflict, so optimizing either degrades the other
causes.commander: services commit independently, so a late failure leaves earlier commits standing with no single transaction to roll back
causes.component: behaviour fixed by class hierarchy cannot be recombined per entity, and subclassing every combination explodes
causes.composite: clients must branch on leaf-versus-container everywhere, so the tree's structure leaks into every operation
causes.composite-entity: managing interdependent persistent objects individually multiplies remote calls and scatters their consistency rules
causes.composite-view: a page assembled inline couples its layout to every part, so no part can change or be reused independently
causes.context-object: protocol-specific state passed as parameters couples every intermediate layer to a protocol it does not use
causes.converter: the same conversion logic is rewritten at every boundary crossing, so the two shapes drift and the conversions disagree
causes.curiously-recurring-template-pattern: a base class cannot name its concrete subclass's type, so fluent returns and static polymorphism need casts
causes.currying: a function demanding all arguments at once cannot be specialised with the ones known early
causes.dao-factory: the choice of storage backend surfaces wherever a DAO is constructed, so switching stores means touching business logic
causes.data-access-object: persistence details woven into business logic make the store's schema and API part of every business change
causes.data-bus: direct references between communicating components form a web that must be rewired for every new participant
causes.data-locality: related data scattered across the heap defeats the cache, so run time is spent waiting on memory rather than computing
causes.data-mapper: an in-memory model mirroring the schema cannot evolve without a matching schema change, and vice versa
causes.data-transfer-object: each fine-grained remote call pays a network round trip, so assembling one result costs many latencies
causes.decorator: subclassing per combination of responsibilities explodes, and inheritance fixes the combination at compile time
causes.delegation: inheriting for reuse imports the whole parent contract when only one behaviour was wanted
causes.dependency-injection: a class that constructs its own collaborators has chosen their concrete types forever, so tests and configurations cannot substitute them
causes.dirty-flag: the derived value's inputs rarely change, but nothing records that fact, so every read pays the recomputation
causes.domain-model: procedural scripts over data duplicate business rules across procedures, and complex rules have no single home
causes.double-buffer: reading a state mid-write shows a torn, partial version — but blocking the writer stalls production
causes.double-checked-locking: taking the lock on every read makes the common case pay for the rare initialisation
causes.double-dispatch: single dispatch selects behaviour on one run-time type, and the correct operation here depends on two
causes.dynamic-proxy: the same cross-cutting wrapper hand-written per interface duplicates code that differs only in the interface
causes.event-aggregator: subscribing to many sources directly couples the listener to each one, and the wiring grows with the product of both sides
causes.event-based-asynchronous: blocking on completion holds the caller's thread; polling for it wastes cycles and adds latency
causes.event-driven-architecture: an emitter that calls its reactors directly must know them all, so every new reaction changes the emitter
causes.event-queue: handling an event at arrival time couples the handler's pace to the arrival rate, which it cannot control
causes.event-sourcing: storing only current state erases how it was reached, so audit, replay and temporal queries are unanswerable
causes.execute-around: setup and teardown are the caller's responsibility, and any forgotten or exception-skipped teardown leaks the resource
causes.extension-objects: anticipating every client's interface in one class bloats it, and late interfaces cannot be added without modifying it
causes.facade: clients must orchestrate many subsystem classes correctly, so the subsystem's internal structure becomes every caller's problem
causes.factory: the knowledge of which concrete type fits which data is branching, and spreading that branching across callers couples all of them to all variants
causes.factory-kit: a factory whose catalogue is fixed in code cannot accept types discovered or configured at run time
causes.factory-method: the creating class would have to name a concrete type it cannot know, foreclosing the subclasses' choice
causes.fallback: propagating a dependency's failure fails the whole request when a degraded answer would have served
causes.fanout-fanin: one worker processing the whole request serially leaves the others idle and makes latency the sum instead of the max
causes.feature-toggle: behaviour bound at build time cannot be switched per environment, tenant or emergency without a redeploy
causes.filterer: filtering criteria fixed inside the container force a new container method for every new predicate
causes.fluent-interface: independent setter calls carry no order or grouping, so misconfiguration reads as well as correct configuration
causes.flux: state mutated from many places has no traceable flow, so a change cannot be followed from trigger to result
causes.flyweight: per-object storage of state that is identical across objects multiplies memory by the object count
causes.front-controller: each entry point re-implements auth, routing and logging, so a policy change must be repeated everywhere
causes.function-composition: combining transformations by hand requires intermediate variables and plumbing that obscure the actual chain
causes.game-loop: simulation driven by input or rendering events runs at an uncontrolled, hardware-dependent rate
causes.gateway: external APIs invoked directly spread the foreign protocol through local code, so a vendor change touches everything
causes.guarded-suspension: failing or spinning on an unmet precondition either loses the request or burns CPU until the state changes
causes.half-sync-half-async: mixing asynchronous arrival with synchronous processing in one layer makes each block the other
causes.health-check: from outside, a hung process and a healthy one look identical until real traffic fails
causes.hexagonal-architecture: business logic that knows its adapters cannot be driven by tests or ported to new technologies without rewriting
causes.identity-map: loading the same record twice yields two objects whose edits diverge silently until one overwrites the other
causes.immutable: shared mutable state can change under any holder, so every reader needs synchronisation and no key is stable
causes.intercepting-filter: pre- and post-processing coded into each handler duplicates policy and cannot be recombined per request
causes.interpreter: sentences of the language handled by ad-hoc parsing scatter grammar knowledge through the code
causes.iterator: exposing the collection's storage couples every traversal to the representation, which then cannot change
causes.layered-architecture: presentation, logic and data access mixed in one class can only be changed, tested or replaced together
causes.lazy-loading: eager loading pulls the object's whole graph for callers who need one field, so cost is set by the heaviest user
causes.leader-election: several identical instances will each perform the job unless exactly one is chosen, and static assignment dies with the assignee
causes.leader-followers: a dispatcher thread handing events to workers becomes the serial bottleneck for every event
causes.lockable-object: a global lock serialises unrelated accesses; per-access locking has no owner and cannot be reasoned about
causes.map-reduce: a single machine cannot hold or process the dataset, and ad-hoc distribution mixes coordination into the computation
causes.marker-interface: a fact about a type carried nowhere testable forces string or reflection checks at every consumer
causes.master-worker: the divisible work has no coordinator, so either one worker does it all or workers must self-organise
causes.mediator: objects referring to each other directly form a web where every interaction change touches several classes
causes.memento: capturing state from outside breaks encapsulation; not capturing it makes undo impossible
causes.metadata-mapping: hand-written mapping code repeats the same field-to-column pattern per class and drifts as the schema moves
causes.microservices-aggregrator: clients calling each service themselves couple to the topology and repeat the assembly logic per client
causes.microservices-api-gateway: clients that know every service's address break on topology changes, and each service re-implements the same edge concerns
causes.microservices-client-side-ui-composition: one team owning the whole page serialises every other team's releases behind its own
causes.microservices-distributed-tracing: each service logs its own hop with no shared correlation, so a failing request cannot be followed across boundaries
causes.microservices-idempotent-consumer: at-least-once delivery means duplicates are normal, and a consumer that applies effects per delivery applies them twice
causes.microservices-log-aggregation: diagnosing one request means opening as many log stores as services it touched
causes.microservices-messaging: synchronous calls couple both services' availability — either being down fails the interaction
causes.microservices-self-registration: instances appear and disappear at run time, so any static address list is stale by construction
causes.model-view-controller: display, input handling and data in one class can only change together, and none can be tested alone
causes.model-view-intent: state mutated directly by handlers cannot be reproduced or reasoned about as a function of what the user did
causes.model-view-presenter: logic living in the view can only be tested by instantiating the UI toolkit
causes.model-view-viewmodel: hand-written view updates must mirror every state change, and the mirroring code is the bug surface
causes.monad: each possibly-absent or possibly-failing step adds a nesting level of conditionals, and the happy path disappears inside them
causes.money: bare numbers carry no currency and no rounding rule, so mixed-currency arithmetic and drift pass silently
causes.monitor: interleaved method executions corrupt the shared invariant, and requiring every caller to lock correctly delegates safety to the least careful one
causes.monolithic-architecture: distribution adds network failure, deployment orchestration and observability cost that a small system never earns back
causes.monostate: a visible singleton forces callers through one instance; yet separate instances with separate state would diverge
causes.multiton: one instance overall is too few and unmanaged instances per key duplicate; nothing enforces one-per-key
causes.mute-idiom: the compiler demands handling for an exception the code can prove impossible, and the handling is pure noise
causes.naked-objects: a hand-written UI mirrors the domain model and must be changed in step with it, twice per concept
causes.notification: throwing on the first validation failure hides the rest, so the user fixes errors one round trip at a time
causes.null-object: an absent collaborator represented as null forces a check at every use, and one missed check is a crash
causes.object-mother: each test hand-builds the same fixtures, so a model change breaks every test's construction code independently
causes.object-pool: construction cost is paid per use even though instances are reusable, and unbounded creation exhausts the resource
causes.observer: a subject that calls its dependents by name is coupled to all of them, so reactions cannot be added without changing it
causes.onion-architecture: dependencies pointing inward-to-infrastructure make the domain depend on technology choices it should survive
causes.optimistic-offline-lock: holding a lock across think time blocks everyone; not detecting concurrent edits silently overwrites the first writer
causes.page-controller: shared request-handling code cannot vary per page, and per-page copies of it drift
causes.page-object: tests addressing the markup directly break on every cosmetic change, in every test that touches the page
causes.parameter-object: the same argument group repeated through signatures means every addition to the group changes every signature
causes.partial-response: returning the full resource to every client sets each response's size by the hungriest consumer
causes.pipeline: stages welded into one procedure cannot be reordered, reused or tested independently
causes.poison-pill: stopping consumers out-of-band races with work still in the queue; the queue itself is the only ordered channel
causes.polling-publisher: the source cannot push, so without deliberate polling its changes are simply never observed
causes.presentation-model: view state entangled with widgets can only be tested through the toolkit, which tests poorly
causes.private-class-data: mutable state exposed after construction lets any collaborator move values that were meant to be fixed
causes.producer-consumer: direct handoff couples the two rates — the faster side stalls on the slower one
causes.promise: a result that does not exist yet cannot be returned, so without a placeholder the caller must block or callback-nest
causes.property: attributes declared in the class are fixed per type, and per-instance additions have nowhere to live
causes.prototype: constructing from scratch repeats expensive initialisation an existing instance has already paid for
causes.proxy: access policy coded into clients spreads it everywhere; coded into the object, it burdens the object with concerns not its own
causes.publish-subscribe: a sender that must know its receivers cannot serve an open, changing set of them
causes.queue-based-load-leveling: bursts hit the service at burst rate, so capacity must be provisioned for the peak instead of the average
causes.rate-limiting-pattern: nothing bounds a caller's request rate, so one client can exhaust a resource shared by all
causes.reactor: a thread per connection exhausts threads long before it exhausts connections
causes.registry: passing well-known objects through every layer threads plumbing through code that never uses them
causes.repository: query logic written inline spreads the schema through domain code and cannot be reused or substituted
causes.resource-acquisition-is-initialization: release coded per exit path misses the path someone adds later, and the resource leaks exactly then
causes.retry: treating a transient failure as final fails work that one more attempt would have completed
causes.role-object: one class carrying every client's interface bloats, and roles fixed at construction cannot be gained later
causes.rule-engine: rules buried in branching can only be changed by programmers, on the code's release cycle — slower than the rules change
causes.saga: without one commit spanning the services, a mid-sequence failure leaves the earlier steps applied and no one to undo them
causes.separated-interface: depending on the implementation's package couples the caller to a layer it is forbidden to know
causes.serialized-entity: field-by-field mapping of an object that is only ever used whole costs schema and code for no query benefit
causes.serialized-lob: a small graph always read together pays joins and mapping for a decomposition nothing queries
causes.servant: the shared behaviour would have to be inherited, but the classes needing it cannot share a parent
causes.server-session: per-client state must survive between requests, and HTTP carries no memory of the client between them
causes.service-layer: each UI re-implements application logic, and without one entry point transaction boundaries sit nowhere
causes.service-locator: constructing collaborators per call repeats costly lookups, and hard-wiring them fixes what deployment must vary
causes.service-stub: a test bound to the real external service inherits its latency, cost and availability
causes.service-to-worker: handlers that both compute and choose views mix dispatch with logic, so neither can change alone
causes.session-facade: each fine-grained call crosses the network, so a workflow's cost is its call count times the latency
causes.sharding: one store's capacity bounds the whole dataset, and past that bound there is nothing a bigger box can do
causes.single-table-inheritance: a table per subclass makes every polymorphic read a join across the hierarchy
causes.singleton: multiple instances of what must be unique diverge, and global reachability by construction is otherwise unregulated
causes.spatial-partition: proximity queries over an unindexed set test every pair, and the pair count grows quadratically
causes.special-case: the same conditional for the exceptional value repeats at every caller, and each copy can disagree
causes.specification: selection rules written per query cannot be combined, reused or tested as rules
causes.state: behaviour branching on a state field spreads the state machine across every method that consults it
causes.step-builder: a builder that allows any call order lets required steps be skipped, and the error surfaces only at build time
causes.strangler: replacing a serving system in one cut risks everything at once, but the legacy cannot simply stop
causes.strategy: algorithm variants branching inside one method couple the chooser to every variant and close the set
causes.subclass-sandbox: subclasses reaching outside for primitive operations couple every subclass to the wider system
causes.table-inheritance: one table for the whole hierarchy nulls out every subclass-specific column and loses per-class constraints
causes.table-module: an object per row adds identity and mapping cost where the logic never varies per object
causes.template-method: implementations sharing a fixed sequence duplicate the sequence, so a change to it must be repeated per implementation
causes.templateview: generating mostly-static markup from code inverts the ratio — the constant part is written inside the varying part
causes.thread-pool-executor: a thread per task pays creation cost per task and unbounded threads exhaust the machine under load
causes.thread-specific-storage: state that must be per-thread has no home: globals are shared, and parameters thread it through every call
causes.throttling: shared capacity with no per-tenant cap lets one tenant's load become every tenant's outage
causes.tolerant-reader: a reader that validates the whole message shape breaks on every addition, coupling it to the sender's release cycle
causes.trampoline: each recursive call consumes a stack frame, and the stack is bounded far below the recursion depth
causes.transaction-script: a domain model's structure costs more to build and navigate than the simple procedures it would replace
causes.twin: the language allows one superclass, and the class needs to stand in two hierarchies
causes.type-object: a class per kind means every new kind is a code change and a release, though kinds differ only in data
causes.unit-of-work: writing each change as it happens interleaves partial states and gives concurrency and ordering nowhere to be enforced
causes.update-method: per-object advancement coded ad hoc couples every object's timing to whoever remembers to call it
causes.value-object: objects compared by identity make equal values unequal, and mutability breaks any equality that was established
causes.version-number: without a version, concurrent updates overwrite each other and the loser never learns it lost
causes.view-helper: logic written in the template can neither be tested nor reused, and grows where nobody reviews it
causes.virtual-proxy: eager construction pays the expensive object's cost even on runs that never touch it
causes.visitor: operations added into the hierarchy's classes change every class per operation, though the hierarchy itself is stable
